reason: The text describes the Israelites' suffering under harsh Egyptian enslavement and depicts God and the designated leaders (Moses and Aaron) responding with compassion and liberation efforts. When the Israelites cry out and groan under oppression, God hears their groaning, remembers His covenant, and instructs Moses and Aaron to lead them to freedom. There is no instance in this passage where the leaders attribute the people's suffering to their own fault or blame them for their condition. Instead, God validates their suffering as real and worthy of divine intervention.
